PostgreSQL and Redis live instances were offline during local audit; isolated static and mock execution harnesses were used for database driver behavior verification.

findings.title: SyntaxError in briefingsApi.exportMarkdown() due to parsing PlainText/HTML response as JSON
affected_components: Weekly review and morning briefing user self-reflection export
findings.root_cause: The frontend helper apiGet unconditionally calls res.json(). However, the backend endpoint /api/analytics/briefing/export returns PlainTextResponse or HTMLResponse. Calling res.json() on raw Markdown or HTML throws a fatal SyntaxError.
findings.expected_behavior: exportMarkdown should fetch and return the raw text or markdown content as a string without passing it to JSON.parse.
findings.actual_behavior: Throws 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token '#', "# Morning "... is not valid JSON' and crashes the calling UI.
reproduction_steps: 1. Start the backend or mock the export endpoint returning Markdown text starting with '# Morning Briefing'.
2. Call briefingsApi.exportMarkdown() in api.ts.
3. Observe uncaught SyntaxError in res.json().
evidence: backend/app/routers/analytics.py line 663: return PlainTextResponse(content=content)
src/services/api.ts line 170: return res.json() as Promise<T>
Verified with Node.js scratch runner: JSON.parse('# Morning Briefing') throws SyntaxError.
findings.impact: Users are completely unable to export their weekly review stories or morning briefings as Markdown; unhandled promise rejection in client.
findings.recommended_fix: Add apiGetText(path: string): Promise<string> in src/services/api.ts that returns res.text() rather than res.json(), and point briefingsApi.exportMarkdown to apiGetText.
regression_tests: Unit test verifying briefingsApi.exportMarkdown parses markdown response as a raw string and does not invoke JSON.parse.
verification_criteria: briefingsApi.exportMarkdown returns valid markdown string starting with '# ' without throwing.

findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in HTML Export Card Generation
findings.root_cause: Raw f-strings are used to construct HTML templates without applying html.escape() to user-controlled variables (user_name, wins, next_rec title and rule).
findings.expected_behavior: All dynamic text injected into HTML documents must be safely HTML-escaped using html.escape() or a secure templating engine.
findings.actual_behavior: Raw strings containing '<script>' or 'onerror=' are rendered unescaped into HTML output.
trigger_conditions: User name, habit title, or experiment challenge containing HTML special characters or tags.
reproduction_steps: 1. Set user_name to '' or create an experiment titled ''.
2. Request GET /api/analytics/briefing/export?export_format=html.
3. Inspect the returned HTML to observe unescaped executable script tags.
evidence: backend/app/ml/insight_synthesizer.py lines 564, 592, 595, 596: user_name and wins concatenated directly into html_card f-string without html.escape.

backend/app/routers/analytics.py line 661: f'...
{content}
...'
findings.impact: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of the user's session or browser when opening exported HTML self-reflection cards.
findings.recommended_fix: Import html and wrap all interpolated dynamic variables in html.escape() before inserting into HTML templates.
regression_tests: Security unit test asserting that input '<script>alert(1)</script>' is escaped to '<script>alert(1)</script>' in html_card output.
verification_criteria: No raw unescaped HTML tags present in generated HTML card from dynamic variables.

findings.title: Mutation Outbox Double Retry Increment & Concurrency Race Condition
findings.root_cause: updateMutationStatus unconditionally increments retry_count by 1 regardless of whether the status is transitioning to IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, or FAILED. Reconcile updates to IN_PROGRESS and then to FAILED/COMPLETED, causing 2 increments per attempt. Furthermore, lack of an isReconciling lock allows parallel calls to drain and execute identical mutations simultaneously.
findings.expected_behavior: retry_count should only increment on failed attempts (status === 'FAILED'). An active reconciliation lock must prevent concurrent execution passes.
findings.actual_behavior: A single failed attempt increases retryCount by 2. Parallel reconciliation passes duplicate requests to the server.
trigger_conditions: Offline mutation reconciliation failure or rapid network status flapping triggering reconcile twice.
reproduction_steps: 1. Enqueue mutation with initial retryCount 0.
2. Run reconcilePendingMutations with a failing sender once.
3. Inspect pending mutation: retryCount is 2 instead of 1.
evidence: src/services/offlineSyncService.ts lines 197-200, 212: retryCount += 1 unconditionally in updateMutationStatus.
Reproduced in scratch harness: single failure yielded retryCount = 2.
findings.impact: Premature expiration of retry thresholds; duplicate mutation execution causing duplicate financial transactions or habit logs.
findings.recommended_fix: Only increment retryCount when status is 'FAILED'. Add private isReconciling = false flag at the top of reconcilePendingMutations.
regression_tests: Test that 1 failed attempt yields retryCount === 1, and successful attempt does not increase retryCount.
verification_criteria: Mutation retryCount strictly equals number of failed attempts; parallel reconcile invocations bail out cleanly.

findings.title: PostgreSQL UUID Datatype Mismatch in Chat Session Queries
findings.root_cause: ChatSession.user_id is mapped as UUID(as_uuid=True). In multiple queries, it is compared directly with string user_id (ChatSession.user_id == user_id). In PostgreSQL with asyncpg, comparing UUID and varchar raises an operator does not exist exception.
findings.expected_behavior: user_id should be converted to uuid.UUID(str(user_id)) before building SQLAlchemy query filter expressions.
findings.actual_behavior: Raises asyncpg.exceptions.DatatypeMismatchError: operator does not exist: uuid = character varying on PostgreSQL.
trigger_conditions: Accessing chat history, deleting sessions, or creating conversations on PostgreSQL.
reproduction_steps: 1. Connect backend to PostgreSQL.
2. Send GET /api/assistant/sessions with valid auth token.
3. Observe SQL execution error comparing UUID column with varchar.
evidence: backend/app/services/assistant_service.py lines 123, 155, 212, 261, 280: ChatSession.user_id == user_id where user_id is type str.
Line 135 correctly converts user_id=uuid.UUID(str(user_id)), proving the model requires UUID.
findings.impact: Complete failure of assistant conversation loading, deletion, and retrieval in PostgreSQL production environments.
findings.recommended_fix: Normalize user_id at the start of every function: uid = uuid.UUID(str(user_id)) and use ChatSession.user_id == uid.
regression_tests: Integration test running against PostgreSQL instance executing get_user_sessions with UUID comparison.
verification_criteria: All chat session queries execute cleanly without type mismatch errors on PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Institutional Webhooks Inoperable due to User Authentication Requirement
findings.root_cause: The webhook endpoint specifies user_id: str = Depends(get_current_user). External webhook providers (Plaid, Finvu) send server-to-server POST requests signed with HMAC headers, not user JWT Bearer tokens.
findings.expected_behavior: Webhook endpoints should authenticate via HMAC signature (x-webhook-signature), and map the institutional account/item ID in the payload to the respective user.
findings.actual_behavior: All external webhook deliveries fail immediately with 401 Unauthorized because external servers lack user Bearer tokens.
trigger_conditions: External webhook dispatch from Plaid or Finvu Account Aggregator.
reproduction_steps: 1. Dispatch a valid HMAC-signed webhook POST to /api/ingestion/financial/webhook without an Authorization Bearer header.
2. Observe immediate 401 Unauthorized rejection.
evidence: backend/app/routers/ingestion.py lines 166-172: user_id: str = Depends(get_current_user) on public webhook route.
findings.impact: Zero institutional transactions can be ingested via webhooks; automated account aggregator sync is completely inoperable.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove Depends(get_current_user) from the webhook route; verify authenticity exclusively via verify_webhook_signature(raw_body, x_webhook_signature) and resolve user via item/account ID.
regression_tests: Test webhook invocation with valid HMAC header and no Authorization header succeeding with 200 OK.
verification_criteria: Webhook requests with valid HMAC signatures authenticate and process without requiring Bearer tokens.

findings.title: Inconsistent Transaction Deduplication Hashes between Client (Polynomial) and Backend (SHA-256)
findings.root_cause: Frontend smsParserService generates hashes using a custom 32-bit polynomial Math.imul hash with date sliced to 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Backend uses Python hashlib.sha256 with full ISO datetime strings. The two algorithms never match for the same physical transaction.
findings.expected_behavior: Frontend and backend must use the exact same canonical normalization format and standard SHA-256 hashing algorithm.
findings.actual_behavior: Transactions parsed on-device via SMS produce different hashes from backend CSV statement and webhook imports, leading to duplicate records.
trigger_conditions: A user logs a transaction via SMS and subsequently uploads a bank statement or receives a bank webhook for the same transaction.
reproduction_steps: 1. Parse SMS 'Spent Rs 450 at Swiggy on 07-Nov-2026' -> produces custom polynomial hash '2e...'.
2. Ingest statement CSV with the same Swiggy transaction -> produces SHA-256 hash 'a7...'.
3. Observe both transactions inserted into database without deduplication.
evidence: src/services/smsParserService.ts lines 245-272 vs backend/app/utils/ingestion_utils.py lines 60-68.
Reproduced in scratch test: algorithms produce completely distinct hash values.
findings.impact: Financial double-counting: discretionary spending ratios and monthly budget overruns are falsely inflated.
findings.recommended_fix: Standardize on SHA-256 (using Web Crypto API or crypto-js on frontend) and canonicalize the input string format identically across platforms.
regression_tests: Cross-platform test asserting that frontend and backend hash functions generate the identical 32-character string for identical transaction parameters.
verification_criteria: Given identical amount, merchant, date, and reference number, frontend and backend yield identical hashes.

findings.title: Date Parsing Month/Day Inversion in Indian Bank Statement CSV Parser
findings.root_cause: parseDateString executes new Date(trimmed) as the primary parser. In JavaScript, date strings like '05/11/2026' are parsed as MM/DD/YYYY (May 11th). Indian bank statements format dates as DD/MM/YYYY (Nov 5th). Because new Date returns a valid date for days 1-12, the DD/MM fallback never executes.
findings.expected_behavior: DD/MM/YYYY date formats from Indian banks must be parsed with day first (day = 5, month = 11).
findings.actual_behavior: Days 1 through 12 of every month have their month and day swapped, writing historical transactions to incorrect months.
trigger_conditions: Importing statement CSV from HDFC, SBI, ICICI, or Axis with dates between the 1st and 12th of any month.
reproduction_steps: 1. Pass '05/11/2026' to parseCsvStatementText.
2. Inspect the resulting transaction timestamp: month is 05 (May) instead of 11 (November).
evidence: src/services/statementParserService.ts lines 128-140.
Scratch runner output: '05/11/2026' -> parsed as May 11th, month=5.
findings.impact: Severe historical data corruption: spending metrics and monthly analytics are shifted by months.
findings.recommended_fix: Explicitly parse DD/MM/YYYY patterns with regex prior to calling generic new Date(), prioritizing DD/MM for Indian statements.
regression_tests: Unit test verifying '05/11/2026' parses as November 5, 2026, and '01/02/2026' parses as February 1, 2026.
verification_criteria: DD/MM/YYYY strings correctly extract day as first token and month as second token.

findings.title: Unhandled JSON Parse Exception in SQLite Native Entity Cache
findings.root_cause: In the native expo-sqlite branch of getCachedEntity, JSON.parse(String(rows[0].data_json)) is called without a try/catch block. In contrast, the AsyncStorage fallback branch wraps JSON.parse in try/catch.
findings.expected_behavior: Corrupted or partial JSON in the database cache should be caught gracefully and return null.
findings.actual_behavior: Throws an unhandled SyntaxError and crashes calling components on native devices.
trigger_conditions: Corrupted data_json column in offline_cache SQLite table.
reproduction_steps: 1. Insert invalid JSON string into offline_cache table.
2. Call getCachedEntity('test', 'key').
3. Observe uncaught SyntaxError in SQLite execution branch.
evidence: src/services/offlineSyncService.ts lines 356-358: return JSON.parse(String(rows[0].data_json)) without try/catch.
findings.impact: Native mobile crash when loading corrupted offline cache data on app launch.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block in the SQLite branch, returning null on parse failure.
regression_tests: Unit test verifying getCachedEntity returns null when database contains corrupted JSON.
verification_criteria: Malformed cached entity JSON safely returns null without throwing.

findings.title: Financial Safety Boundary Bypassed for Tool Execution and Card Rendering
findings.root_cause: check_crisis_boundary and check_medical_boundary are intercepted before tool execution in run_conversational_agent. check_financial_boundary was omitted from early interception. It runs tools (such as get_spending_breakdown), and although the content text is replaced by the guardrail filter, the executed tools and UI cards are returned and rendered.
findings.expected_behavior: Financial speculation queries must intercept early, executing zero tools and returning zero cards, identical to crisis and medical queries.
findings.actual_behavior: Tool execution occurs and private spending cards are returned alongside the deflection message.
trigger_conditions: User asks a speculative financial query that contains keywords matching tool intents (e.g. 'Which stock should I buy for my spending?').
reproduction_steps: 1. Send user message 'Where should I invest my money from my spend?'.
2. Observe get_spending_breakdown tool executes and cards are returned in response payload.
evidence: backend/app/ai/agent.py lines 25, 260-279 vs 302.
Scratch script confirmed tool execution count = 1 on speculative financial prompt.
findings.impact: Violation of AI guardrail contract; private financial data cards leaked on restricted queries.
findings.recommended_fix: Add financial_resp = check_financial_boundary(user_message) to early boundary interception in agent.py.
regression_tests: Adversarial test asserting speculative financial queries return tools_to_run === [] and cards === [].
verification_criteria: Speculative investment inquiries return zero tool calls and zero cards.

findings.title: MediaRecorder Audio Blob Truncation on Web Platform
findings.root_cause: stopWebRecording invokes this.webMediaRecorder.stop() and immediately reads this.webAudioChunks on the subsequent synchronous line without awaiting the asynchronous dataavailable and stop events.
findings.expected_behavior: stopWebRecording must await a Promise resolving on the MediaRecorder 'stop' event to ensure all audio buffers have flushed.
findings.actual_behavior: Final audio buffers are not included in webAudioChunks, creating truncated or empty 0-byte audio blobs.
reproduction_steps: 1. Start web recording in browser.
2. Speak for 2 seconds and tap stop.
3. Inspect returned blob: webAudioChunks is empty and falls back to dummy 1024-byte sine wave.
evidence: src/services/voiceService.ts lines 272-289: synchronous read of webAudioChunks after recorder.stop().
findings.impact: Speech recognition failures on Web platform; voice assistant transcribes noise or empty inputs.
findings.recommended_fix: Wrap recorder.stop() in an await new Promise(resolve => recorder.addEventListener('stop', resolve, { once: true })).
regression_tests: Web test asserting stopWebRecording waits for recorder stop event before creating Blob.
verification_criteria: Recorded audio blob on web retains full duration and all data chunks.

findings.title: Circadian Streak Persistence and Lag-1 Correlation Across Missing Data Gaps
findings.root_cause: In detect_circadian_drift, consecutive_delay_count is only reset in the else branch of 'diff >= 60'. If days are non-contiguous, the loop skips without resetting the counter. In dynamic_correlation, lag-1 loop pairs entries[i-1] and entries[i] by array index without verifying date difference equals 1 day.
findings.expected_behavior: Missing days between entries must break consecutive streaks, and lag-1 correlations must only pair records that are exactly 1 calendar day apart.
findings.actual_behavior: Phase delay streaks carry over multi-day tracking gaps, and lag-1 correlations falsely associate events separated by weeks.
trigger_conditions: User skips tracking for several days after an initial late night, then logs another late night.
reproduction_steps: 1. Provide bedtimes on Day 0 and Day 1 (+75m shift).
2. Leave Days 2-5 unlogged.
3. Provide bedtime on Day 6 (+75m shift from Day 5).
4. Observe consecutive_drift_days evaluates to 2 instead of 1.
evidence: backend/app/ml/risk_forecaster.py lines 453-460.
Reproduced in Python scratch script: consecutive_drift_days = 2 despite multi-day gap.
findings.impact: False-positive circadian phase delay alerts and flawed behavioral correlation insights.
findings.recommended_fix: Reset consecutive_delay_count = 0 when curr_idx != prev_idx + 1; verify date(curr) - date(prev) == timedelta(days=1) in lag-1 correlation.
regression_tests: Unit test verifying non-contiguous entries reset the consecutive delay streak to 0.
verification_criteria: Streaks and lag-1 correlations strictly enforce calendar day adjacency.

findings.title: Hardcoded User Spending/Name and Month-To-Date Date Window Truncation
findings.root_cause: get_or_create_morning_briefing hardcodes current_spend=12400.0, monthly_budget=35000.0, and user_name='Priya'. get_composite_risk_forecasts queries entries with date >= ref_date - 14 days, truncating MTD spending for days 1 to 17 on the second half of every month.
findings.expected_behavior: Briefings should query the user's actual name and financial transactions/entries from the first day of the current month.
findings.actual_behavior: All users receive hardcoded financial values and 'Priya' in generated briefings; MTD spending is truncated after mid-month.
trigger_conditions: Generating morning briefing or weekly review on any date past the 14th of the month.
reproduction_steps: 1. Create user with name 'Alex' and transactions totaling ₹25,000 across November 1–25.
2. Call get_morning_briefing on Nov 25.
3. Observe greeting uses 'Priya' and spend uses hardcoded ₹12,400.
evidence: backend/app/services/briefing_service.py lines 179-181, 197, 340, 408, 433.
findings.impact: Users see fabricated spend and incorrect names in AI briefings, destroying user trust in analytics.
findings.recommended_fix: Query User table for full_name; query FinancialTransaction / DailyEntry starting from date(ref_date.year, ref_date.month, 1).
regression_tests: Test verifying user with custom name and transactions on Day 1 of month correctly reflects in briefing generated on Day 28.
verification_criteria: User full_name is rendered in briefings and MTD calculation spans from day 1 to target date.

findings.title: N+1 Database Query Overhead in Chat Session Listing
findings.root_cause: In get_user_sessions, for each session returned, two separate queries (COUNT messages and SELECT last message) are executed in a loop.
findings.expected_behavior: Session message counts and last message content should be fetched in a single grouped SQL query or window function.
findings.actual_behavior: Generates 1 + 2N database roundtrips per page load (41 queries for 20 sessions).
trigger_conditions: User opening conversation drawer with 10+ chat sessions.
reproduction_steps: 1. Create 20 chat sessions with messages.
2. Call GET /api/assistant/sessions?page_size=20.
3. Observe 41 distinct database queries in SQL query logs.
evidence: backend/app/services/assistant_service.py lines 164-184: queries executed inside for s in sessions loop.
findings.impact: Database latency spikes and connection pool exhaustion as user conversation history grows.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a correlated subquery, LEFT JOIN with GROUP BY, or SQLAlchemy selectinload to aggregate message counts and latest messages in a single query.
regression_tests: Performance test asserting get_user_sessions executes <= 2 queries regardless of page_size.
verification_criteria: Chat session drawer loads in a single aggregated database query.

findings.title: Circadian Late-Night Hour Definition Mismatch between Backend and Specs
findings.root_cause: Backend ingestion_service line 265 evaluates is_late as 'hr >= 22 or hr < 5', which excludes hour 5 (05:00 to 05:59). Frontend tests and specs define late-night as 22:00 to 05:59 (hr < 6).
findings.expected_behavior: Consistent classification of 05:00-05:59 across frontend and backend.
findings.actual_behavior: Screen time sessions at 05:30 AM are marked as daytime by backend ingestion, but marked as late-night by frontend validators.
trigger_conditions: Device usage logged between 05:00 AM and 05:59 AM.
reproduction_steps: 1. Ingest session with start_time '2026-11-04T05:30:00'.
2. Observe is_late_night stored as False in backend database, while frontend test asserts True.
evidence: backend/app/services/ingestion_service.py line 265 vs test/phase1_telemetry.test.mjs line 184.
findings.impact: Minor inconsistency in late-night screen time aggregation across client and server.
regression_tests: Test verifying 05:30 AM session is classified as late night across all services.
verification_criteria: Both client and server classify 22:00 to 05:59 as circadian late-night.

findings.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) Leading Whitespace and Stream Token Splitting Flaw
findings.root_cause: In chat_stream_endpoint, chunks yield json.dumps({'token': ' ' + ' '.join(chunk)}). For the very first chunk emitted, an unwanted leading space is prepended. Furthermore, splitting solely on space (' ') strips indentation.
findings.expected_behavior: The first streamed token must not have a prepended space, and whitespace formatting should be preserved.
findings.actual_behavior: Streamed text begins with an unnatural leading space and loses block indentation.
trigger_conditions: Consuming the SSE chat stream endpoint.
reproduction_steps: 1. Connect to /api/assistant/chat/stream?message=hello.
2. Inspect first 'event: token' event: data starts with a leading space.
evidence: backend/app/routers/assistant.py line 119: {'token': ' ' + ' '.join(chunk)}.
findings.impact: Cosmetic text rendering defect in streaming chat view.
findings.recommended_fix: Only prepend a space for chunks after the first, or split using regex matching word boundaries while retaining leading whitespace.
regression_tests: Test asserting concatenated SSE stream tokens exactly equal the original response string.
verification_criteria: Concatenated tokens perfectly match original markdown without leading space.

findings.title: Offline Outbox Engine Disconnected from Application Network Layer
findings.root_cause: offlineSyncService was implemented as a standalone engine with tests in test/phase7_verification.test.mjs, but was never integrated into api.ts. When network requests fail in apiPost or apiPut, errors are thrown directly to the UI rather than queueing into the outbox.
findings.expected_behavior: When isOnline is false or fetch throws network error (TypeError / ECONNREFUSED), mutations (transactions, habit logs, check-ins) should automatically enqueue into offlineSyncService outbox.
findings.actual_behavior: Mutations fail immediately with an unhandled network error, leaving user data unsaved.
trigger_conditions: User creates a habit log, financial transaction, or experiment check-in while offline.
reproduction_steps: 1. Put client in offline mode.
2. Submit new transaction via + Spend.
3. Observe request throws TypeError: fetch failed and no record is added to offlineSyncService.
evidence: src/services/api.ts: zero imports of offlineSyncService.
Grep across src/ confirms offlineSyncService is only exported, never consumed.
findings.impact: Offline-first capability is completely non-functional for user data entry in real app usage.
findings.recommended_fix: In api.ts, intercept network failures in mutation helpers and automatically enqueue them into offlineSyncService, returning an optimistic success payload.
regression_tests: Integration test asserting apiPost enqueues mutation into offlineSyncService when network fails.
verification_criteria: Failed network mutations successfully persist into outbox and reconcile when online.
